scope: Independent HOST source review for PR 2187 comment 4354993843; no app edits, compilation, device, ADB, GitHub mutation, or push by this reviewer.
recommendation: The one-file simplification is suitable to push for CI and reviewer consideration. This report is source analysis, not an exact-source runtime or whole-app pass.

findings.conclusion: super.setText is unconditionally the first statement. No old text read or comparison precedes it. Nullable normalization and BufferType conversions remain delegated to TextView on every call, including equal-content calls.

The override invokes the parent and then writes only primitive dirty flags; it never reads or dereferences the subclass Paint.FontMetrics or Rect caches during TextView construction. The subclass flag initializers are also true after superclass construction. No new constructor cache dereference was introduced.

findings.topic: Measurement and draw order in ordinary framework paths
findings.conclusion: The reviewed API21 and API35 setText paths may synchronously normalize/filter text, update TextView text/transformation state, initialize movement, rebuild its framework Layout, and notify listeners. Their ordinary relayout/invalidation paths request later traversal; no direct call to AutoScaleTextView.onMeasure or onDraw was found in those ordinary paths. The post-super flags therefore conservatively invalidate custom caches before the requested traversal on the current call paths.

API35 View requestLayout lines 27995-28021, ViewRootImpl requestLayout lines 2471-2477 and scheduleTraversals lines 2888-2893

findings.conclusion: Search of current app/src/main plus the AutoScale consumer implementations found no project TextWatcher, InputFilter, custom TransformationMethod, MovementMethod, or platform auto-size registration on these labels. The only doAfterTextChanged found is on the independent TestInputPanel editor. Standard TextView single-line transformation is used by some labels; this is not a claim that all framework transformations or callbacks are absent.

This is not a universal no-reentrancy guarantee: TextWatcher/filter/transformation/movement callbacks execute synchronously and can run arbitrary client code. A future custom callback that explicitly measures or draws inside super.setText would need its own analysis. No such registration was found in the current AutoScale consumers, and no existing-path need for dirty-before-super was identified.

findings.conclusion: Removing the content comparison intentionally dirties both custom caches and requests layout/redraw even for equal content. This is simpler and conservative for correctness, including buffer-only calls. It may add work on repeated equal assignments; no zero-cost or performance-improvement claim is supported by this source review. Existing measured performance on the previous commit is not automatically evidence for this commit.

Saving an old-content comparison before super would conflict with the literal parent-first request and preserve optional equality logic without a demonstrated need. Comparing content after the parent usually compares against its new value, so it is not a reliable substitute for an old-content comparison. Unconditional dirty flags avoid that issue.

This commit does not change custom measurement/drawing or the retained super.onMeasure and absent super.onLayout. The current review does not relabel prior evidence for those choices as a new execution.

limitations: No assertion that the previous dirty-before-super order caused an observed product bug.
No assertion that arbitrary future synchronous callbacks or reentrant client code are safe.
No exact-source runtime/CI execution claimed by this reviewer. The root independently owns compilation/CI evidence.
No global warning-free, performance-neutral, or zero-risk claim.
